# Aim

In this exercise you will create exploratory scatterplots with `ggplot2`.

By the end, you should have loaded a data file, inspected its variables, completed basic `ggplot()` code, and written short interpretations of the plots you created.

# Improve the Same Plot

The next code chunk starts from the same variables as Figure \@ref(fig:hand-scatter). Instead of rebuilding the plot several times, complete the additions that make the plot easier to read.

Fill in the blanks to:

- make the points slightly transparent,
- add a linear trend line,
- add clearer axis labels.

```{r improved-scatter, fig.cap="Dominant-hand and non-dominant-hand reaction time with clearer labels and a trend line."}
# The x- and y-variables are already filled in.
# alpha controls point transparency. Use a value between 0 and 1, such as 0.6.
# method tells geom_smooth() which trend line to fit. Use "lm" for a linear model.
ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = rt_hand_d, y = rt_hand_nd)) +
  geom_point(alpha = ___) +
  geom_smooth(method = "___", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Dominant-hand reaction time (ms)",
    y = "Non-dominant-hand reaction time (ms)"
  )
```

Compare Figure \@ref(fig:hand-scatter) and Figure \@ref(fig:improved-scatter). What changed?

The improved plot is easier to read because ...

# Use Colour Carefully

Colour can add information, but it should be used for a reason.

In Figure \@ref(fig:colour-scatter), the x- and y-variables are already filled in. Complete the code so the points are coloured by smoking status.

```{r colour-scatter, fig.cap="Reaction time by smoking status."}
# colour adds a visual grouping variable.
# Replace ___ with smoker so each point is coloured by smoking status.
ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = rt_hand_d, y = rt_hand_nd, colour = ___)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(
    x = "Dominant-hand reaction time (ms)",
    y = "Non-dominant-hand reaction time (ms)",
    colour = "Smoking status"
  )
```

Write one sentence describing whether the colour mapping helps interpretation.

The colour mapping is useful / not useful because ...

# Choose Different Variables

Now create a different scatterplot. Use age on the x-axis and dominant-hand reaction time on the y-axis.

Then decide whether the plot should include a trend line.

```{r age-scatter, fig.cap="Age and dominant-hand reaction time."}
# Create a new plot.
# Replace the first ___ with age.
# Replace the second ___ with rt_hand_d.
ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = ___, y = ___)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Dominant-hand reaction time (ms)"
  )
```
